MINUTES
  7’
  MALIBU CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING
  SEPTEMBER 11, 2023
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  5:45 P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant t0 AB 361 and teleconferenced from various
locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Silverstein called the meeting to order at 5:46 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Bruce Silverstein; Mayor Pro Tem Steve Uhring; and Councilmembers
  Paul Grisanti (arrived at 5:47 p.m.), Marianne Riggins, and Doug Stewart

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION

  Mayor Silverstein opened the floor t0 public comment.

  Speakers: None.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION

  At 5:47 p.m., the Council recessed to Closed Session to discuss the following items listed
  on the Closed Session agenda:

Conference with Legal Counsel — Anticipated litigation

  1.  Initiation of litigation pursuant to paragraph (4) of subdivision (d) of Government
  Code section 54956.9
  Number of potential cases: (2)

, REGULAR SESSION CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Silverstein Called the meeting to order at 6:30 pm.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Bruce Silverstein; Mayor Pro Tem Steve Uhring; and Councilmembers
  Paul Grisanti, Marianne Riggins, and Doug Stewart
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of September 11, 2023
  Page 2 of 12

  ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin, Interim City Attorney; Steve McClary, City Manager;
  Alexis Brown, Deputy City Manager; Kelsey Pettijohn, City Clerk; Kristin Riesgo,
  Community Services Director; Yolanda Bundy, Environmental Sustainability Director;
  Richard Mollica, Flaming Director; Susan Dueflas, Public Safety Director; Rob DuBoux,
  Public Works Director; Jason Lawrence, Deputy City Clerk; Christina Munoz, Deputy City
  Clerk; Tracey Rossine, Environmental Programs Manager; Doug Cleavenger, Code
  Enforcement Manager; Tyler Eaton, Senior Planner; Joyce Parker-Bozylinski, Contract
  Planner; Gabriel Etcheverry, Fire Safety Liaison; Sarah Flores, Emergency Services
  Coordinator; Jerry Vandermeulen, Fire Safety Liaison; and Bradley Yocum, Fire Safety
  Liaison

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Beth Grimes led the Pledge of Allegiance.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  Interim City Attorney Rusin reported that the meeting convened at 5:45 p.m., after which
  time the City Council recessed to a Closed Session pursuant to Government Code Section
  54956.9(d)(2), with all Councilmembers present. He stated the Council discussed the item
  listed on the closed session agenda and took no reportable action.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  City Clerk Pettijohn reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted on
  August 31, 2023, with the amended agenda posted on September 8, 2023.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Uhring moved, and Councilmember Riggins seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda and adjourn in memory of those who perished in the terrorist
  attacks on September 11, 2001 and from injuries that occurred on that day. The
  question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.
ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  A.  Proclamation Declaring September 17—September 23, 2023 Constitution Week

  Mayor Silverstein presented the proclamation to Beth Grimes and the Daughters of
  the American Revolution.

  Beth Grimes, Malibu Chapter President of Daughters of the American Revolution,
  introduced fellow members and provided an overview of their organization’s
  mission and history of Constitution Week.

  B.  Presentation on Fire Season Preparedness

  Public Safety Manager Susan Duefias, Fire Safety Liaison Vandermeulen, and
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of September 11, 2023
  Page 3 of 12

  Emergency Services Coordinator Flores provided a presentation on Fire Season
  Preparedness.

  The Council directed questions to staff.

  Presentation on Coastal Vulnerability Proj ect

  Environmental Sustainability Director Bundy and James Jackson, Environmental
  Science Associates, provided a presentation on the Coastal Vulnerability Proj ect

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Joe Sichta, Malibu Aquatics Foundation, discussed the foundation’s operations in
  the community, the decision to terminate the coach, and requirements of the coach
  position. He discussed the competing group Malibu Marlins that formed with
  former Seawolves coach Erik Ran.

  Scott Dittrich discussed the importance of public safety, litigation between
  Southern Califomia Edison (SCE) and the City of Norco to underground power
  lines, and the fire danger posed by overhead power lines. He discussed the
  importance of cleaning Las Flores Creek from a community pride and public safety
  standpoint and stated that the City should get Los Angeles County involved.

  Hans Laetz stated KBUU was now solar powered. He discussed the 1993 Malibu
  fire and problems reporting emergency alerts through KNX in the past, the City’s
  efforts to develop its own radio station, and his role developing KBUU. He
  discussed radio reception challenges and the need for a transmitter signal booster.

  Shamira Strange deferred time to Brian Strange.

  Brian Strange discussed the Formula Retail Ordinance and James Perse’s current
  space in the Malibu Lumber Yard. He discussed the characteristics of formula retail
  as defined by the ordinance and stated multiple stores owned by James Perse shared
  the same characteristics and distracted from Malibu’s variety and unique charm.

  Ingrid Jensen deferred time to Debra Bianco.

  Debra Bianco discussed the Cornucopia Foundation and the farmers’ market
  contributions to the community such as education, operation after emergencies, and
  during challenges presented by the COVID-l9 pandemic and Santa Monica College
  construction. She discussed the organization’s environmental projects and animal
  rescue efforts and the market’s growth since it moved to Legacy Park.

  Sherman Bailard discussed increased visitors to Legacy Park by those who
  discovered it from attending the farmers’ market and hoped for its continued
  operation at the park.

  Ryan Embree commended the City Manager and Public Safety staff for
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of September 11, 2023
  Page 4 of 12

  achievements since he was part of the Emergency Preparedness Task Force. He
  commented on public safety hazards caused by homeless encampments and
  inquired when they would be dismantled.

  Matthew Straeb encouraged the Council to consider the Alert FM system apart from
  the outdoor warning siren proj ect and discussed how Alert FM operated when cell
  service and electrical power were not available. He stated that additional radio
  stations could be used to help provide full coverage of emergency messages and
  discussed a timeline for implementation and potential funding sources.

  Bill Sampson discussed reasons individuals would need to participate in public
  meetings via Zoom. He discussed short-term rentals operating on his street. He
  discussed swim groups and his experience swimming with coach Erik Ran and
  stated that a new non-competitive program should not be at the expense of the
  existing program under the new coach. He discussed challenges the triathlon posed
  and requested access provisions for residents.

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION / COMMITTEE / CITY MANAGER UPDATES

  City Manager McClary stated the California Coastal Commission (CCC) approved
  the City’s modified application for Malibu High School and Middle School Local
  Coastal Program Amendment Specific Plan and the matter would be brought back
  before the City Council on October 9, 2023. He stated the Flaming Commission
  approved the Coastal Development Permit for Phase One ofthe school campus. He
  announced the City received the Certificate of Achievement for Excellence in
  Financial Reporting by the Government Finance Officers Association for its
  Annual Comprehensive Financial Report for the 22nd consecutive year. He reported
  the Sheriff Department beach team concluded its activities Labor Day weekend and
  during the season issued 1,108 citations for alcohol on the beach and made one
  felony and six misdemeanor arrests. He stated that they issued 883 citations for
  hazardous traffic situations, 4,121 parking citations, and towed 513 vehicles. He
  stated that an arrest was made in the stabbing homicide that occurred at Las Tunas
  Beach. He announced California Coastal Cleanup Day would be held on September
  23, 2023 and invited the community to participate in Heal the Bay’s cleanup events
  at Zuma Lagoon and Westward Beach. He discussed an item on an upcoming Los
  Angeles County Board of Supervisors meeting agenda to address illegal street
  takeovers and racing in unincorporated Los Angeles County. He announced’the
  Council reorganization would be held at the September 25, 2023 meeting.

  Sergeant Chris Soderlund, Los Angeles County Sheriff Department, reported there
  were no maj or issues over Labor Day weekend and stated that the chaperone policy
  that required adult supervision of children upon entry to the Chili Cookoff event
  was helpful. He provided crime statistics for August 2023 and stated there were 3 14
  part one crimes year to date as compared to 331 at the same time last year which
  represented a 5.1 percent decrease. He provided information on crimes, none of
  which were committed by Malibu residents. He stated that a robbery and assault
  was reported on Malibu Road where jewelry was stolen, and the suspects were at
  large. He stated an assault was reported on Malibu Road where a vehicle was struck,
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of September 11, 2023
  Page 5 of 12

  and the suspect was arrested. He stated a separate assault was reported 0n Malibu
  Road and the suspect was apprehended. He reported a residential burglary occurred
  on Malibu Road and the suspects were arrested. He provided a summary of
  activities by the afternoon special assignment deputies. He stated that the welfare
  of multiple individuals experiencing homelessness was checked and quality of life
  citations issued. He stated that a felony domestic violence suspect was taken into
  custody at Westward Beach. He stated that they assisted in the incident that
  occurred on the Pepperdine campus and conducted patrols in the area around the
  Chili Cookoff event. He stated that they were on the Sheriff’ s response team which
  was a county-wide unit, and they were deployed to Catalina Island during the
  tropical storm and assisted in evacuation preparations had they become necessary.
  He provided a summary of activities by the overnight special assignment deputies.
  He reported that they conducted foot patrols of Legacy Park and the Malibu Library
  area and spoke to individuals experiencing homelessness and gathered intelligence
  of who was new in town and what was going on with the transient population. He
  stated that they contacted people parked along Coastline, Topanga, and the Malibu
  Pier and counseled them and warned them about illegal parking violations there.
  He stated that six felony and ten misdemeanor arrests were made. He stated that
  they made an animal abuse warrant arrest, a disturbing the peace warrant arrest at
  Legacy Park, a drunk driving and concealed weapon arrest at PCH and Coastline
  Drive, and public urination arrest at PCH and Old Malibu Road. He stated that they
  arrested a suspect for driving a stolen vehicle with an altered vehicle identification
  number that would possibly lead to a chop shop in Los Angeles. He reported that
  the beach team ended full time Labor Day weekend but would continue to have a
  presence on weekends throughout September. He reported that the Council
  received calls about people having dogs on the beach and that 52 citations were
  issued.

  In response to Mayor Silverstein, he stated that the increase in violent crime during
  the summer months was common, but also attributable to the zero-bail policy. He
  stated that the special assignment deputies were directed to address the increase in
  crime along Malibu Road and that there were a high number ofpeople experiencing
  homelessness parked behind the shopping area on Malibu Road and that could be
  contributing to the increase in crime.

ITEM 2.C.  SUBCOMMITTEE REPORTS / COUNCIL COMMENTS

  Councilmember Grisanti stated that he appreciated the emails he received from the
  public and thanked the Fire Safety Liaisons, Environmental Sustainability
  Department staff, and Code Enforcement Manager Cleavenger for their work.

  Councilmember Stewart discussed the expansion of the Public Safety Department
  since the 2018 Woolsey Fire from a one-person division to a more staffed, better
  prepared, and trained department with the ability to perform in a FEMA-compliant
  manner. He suggested Homeowners Association fee reduction incentives for home
  ignition assessments would encourage participation. He expressed support for the
  Alert‘FM system and discussed the importance of having adequate insurance. He
  discussed the importance of enforcement as a tool for compliance. He announced
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of September 11, 2023
  Page 6 of 12

  Jeffrey Jennings’ resignation from the Flaming Commission once a replacement
  was appointed, discussed his contributions to the City, and encouraged interested
  parties to apply. He discussed Executive Assistant Mary Linden’s retirement and
  her 20 years ofcontributions to the City. He stated that he watched the CCC meeting
  on the MHS project and thanked City and School Board staff for their efforts. He
  commented on the tragic events of September 11, 2001, and expressed appreciation
  for Pepperdine University’s annual flag memorial.

  Councilmember Riggins stated she attended the monthly Clean Power Alliance
  meeting and the California Contract Cities Annual Fall Conference. She announced
  Point Dume Preservationist weed pulling event on September 13, 2023 and
  encouraged community participation. She encouraged the public to take emergency
  preparedness actions, including charging batteries, backup power for cellphones,
  keep vehicles full of fuel, know their evacuation zone, have an emergency contact
  outside of the city, have a family evacuation, organize important papers, and have
  medications available.

  Mayor Pro Tem Uhring stated that he attended a meeting with California Strategies.

  In response to Mayor Pro Tem Uhring, City Manager McClary stated that the Zuma
  underpass was not cleared of debris and was unusable. Public Works Director
  DuBouX stated that he would follow up with the Department of Beaches and
k,n. _
  Harbors on solutions. City Manager McClary stated that the matter would be
  discussed at the next Pacific Coast Highway (PCH) Task Force meeting.

  Mayor Pro Tem Uhring discussed school enrollment trends in Malibu. He discussed
  the Malibu Lumber Yards ownership, management, and history, and stated that they
  must be compliant with the City’s ordinances, including the Formula Retail
  Ordinance. He requested an analysis of the terminated leases at the Lumber Yard
  and some assurance that the Formula Retail Ordinance was enforced at the Lumber
  Yard and other businesses in the City.

  Mayor Silverstein requested public submit written correspondence before the day
  ofthe meeting. He discussed Senator Scott Wiener’s Senate Bills No. 423, 424, and
  593 that would remove substantial local authority over multi—family construction.
  He discussed public safety improvements made in recent years. He discussed an
  adjourned item on the CCC agenda for an appeal of a City Council approval of a
  project on a bluffs edge that he opposed and stated that during his research of the
  item he was informed that it was likely the CCC would recommend reversal of the
  approval. He discussed weekend traffic near Malibu Pier and Nobu and stated the
  former Hertz lot was filled with cars, despite not having received approval for
  offsite parking for the Malibu Inn, and requested investigation of the matter. In
  response to Ms. Drummond and Mr. Sampson, he stated While he appreciated being
  informed of what was occurring, private decisions by private organizations about
  employment issues were not within the Council’s purview. He stated that
  swimming pool usage by community organizations was determined by City staff
  using what he assumed were required standards. In response to Mr. Dittrich, he
  stated SCE would not go through the expense of undergrounding. in response to
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of September 11, 2023
  Page 7 of 12

  pressure from the City, but if there was a lawsuit that was successful elsewhere
  against SCE, that possibility should be explored. In response to Mr. Laetz, he stated
  that the Alert FM option should be pursued. In response to Mr. Strange, he stated
  that he researched the Formula Retail Ordinance and stated that it was problematic,
  and he would talk more about it during the ADU ordinance discussion. In response
  to public comment, he stated that there was much support for the continuation of
  the farmers’ market at Legacy Park, however, it was deed restricted and they had
  no authority to override that restriction.

  Councilmember Riggins suggested a business license program be considered by the
  City for more control over what businesses operated in the city.

ITEM 3  CONSENT CALENDAR

  Item Nos. 3.A. l. and 3.B.6. were pulled by the public.

MOTION  Councilmember Riggins moved, and Councilmember Grisanti seconded a motion
  to approve the Consent Calendar, pulling Item Nos. 3.A. l. and 3.B.6. The question
  was called, and the motion carried unanimously, Councilmembers Riggins and
  Stewart abstaining from Item No. 3.B.3.

  names, for the purposes stated on the respective demands in a total amount
  of $749,004.09. City of Malibu payroll check number 5368-5370 and ACH

  3.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes for the October 10, 2022

  4.  Findings to Hold Virtual City Council, Commission, Committee, Board and

  Recommended Action: Consider a motion to reaffirm Resolution No. 23-
  14, re—authorizing remote teleconferencing/virtual meetings pursuant to AB
  361 .
  5.  Professional Services Agreement with Iris Consulting

  Recommended Action: Authorize the Mayor to execute the Professional
  Services Agreement with Iris Consulting for software development and
  system integration.
  7.  Amendment No. 2 to Agreement with Environmental Science Associates
  for the Coastal Vulnerability Assessment
  Recommended Action: Authorize the Mayor to execute Amendment No. 2
  to agreement with Environmental Science Associates to: l) increase the

  increase the total compensation for services.

  The following items were pulled from the consent calendar for individual consideration:

  A.  Previously

  1.  Second Reading and Adoption of Ordinance No. 509
  Recommended Action: Conduct second reading, unless waived, and adopt
  Ordinance N0. 509, an ordinance of the City of Malibu amending Zoning
  Map Amendment (ZMA) No. 17-002 and Zoning Text Amendment (ZTA)
  No. 20-001 to effectuate previous amendments made to Local Coastal

  as adopted by Ordinance No. 491 on September 13, 2021 and amended by
  Ordinance No. 508 on July 10, 2023 pursuant to the conditional certification
  action taken by the Califomia Coastal Commission (CCC) on February 8,
  2023 to rezone and change the land use designation ofthe properties located
  at 22741 and 22729 Pacific Coast Highway from Community Commercial

ITEM 5 ,  OLD BUSINESS

  Woolsey Fire Fee Waiver Program and Rebuild Deadlines
  . Recommended Action: 1) Consider adopting Resolution No. 23-40 superseding
  and replacing Resolution No. 21-62, directing the City Manager to waive certain
  fees related to the rebuilding‘of structures that were damaged or destroyed by the
  Woolsey Fire on a property used as a primary residence; 2) Consider adopting
  Resolution No. 23-41 initiating a Zoning Text Amendment (ZTA) to modify
  Malibu Municipal Code (MMC) Section 17.60.020(C) to extend the submittal
  deadline for owners to obtain a permit for Planning Verification approvals for
  nonconforming structures damaged or destroyed in the Woolsey Fire; and 3) If
  Resolution No. 23-41 is adopted, direct the Flaming Commission to schedule a
  public hearing regarding the same.

  Environmental Sustainability Director Bundy and Flaming Director Mollica
  presented the staff report.
  The Council directed questions to staff.

  Mayor Silverstein opened the floor to public comment.

  Speakers: Armen Hagobian and Ryan Embree

  As there were no other speakers present, Mayor Silverstein returned the matter to
  the table for discussion.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

MOTION  Mayor Silverstein moved, and Mayor Pro Tem Uhring seconded a motion directing
  staff to bring back a resolution extending Woolsey Fire Fee Waiver deadlines three
  years.

  The Council discussed the motion and directed questions to staff.

  The question was called and the motion carried unanimously.

MOTION  Mayor Silverstein moved, and Councilmember Stewart seconded a motion to: 1)
  adopt Resolution No. 23-41 initiating a Zoning Text Amendment (ZTA) to modify
  Malibu Municipal Code (MMC) Section 17.60.020(C) to extend the submittal
  deadline for owners to obtain a permit for Planning Verification approvals for
  nonconforming structures damaged or destroyed in the Woolsey Fire by three years;
  and 2) direct the Planning Commission to schedule a public hearing regarding the
  ZTA. The question was called and the motion carried 4-1, Councilmember Riggins
  opposed.

MOTION  Mayor Silverstein moved, and Councilmember Stewart seconded a motion to
  continue Item Nos. 6.A. and 6.B. to the September 25, 2023 Regular City Council
